public_rationale: The distinctive factual claim is that big tech firms were having to calm down their salespeople about generative AI. In March 2024, The Information reported that representatives of major cloud providers were 'tempering expectations with their salespeople', saying the hype had outrun what the technology could do at a reasonable price. Staff at Microsoft, AWS and Google cited high running costs and accuracy shortcomings. That covers both the 'unprofitable' (costly) and 'unreliable' parts. CNBC's report that AI added 7 points to Azure growth shows it was selling cloud compute, as he said. Google's own admission of inaccurate AI Overviews in May 2024 adds to the reliability point. The claim's core holds. The original article is paywalled and was read through a verbatim reproduction.
limitations: The key evidence is a blog reproducing a paywalled news report.
'Remarkably unprofitable' is not measured with a specific profit figure.
The same report reportedly also said AWS urged salespeople to keep selling generative AI. That nuance could not be read directly.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI is a trend with an actual product, a superficially impressive doodad that can sell cloud compute access and proliferate more software, even though the underlying technology is so unprofitable and unreliable that big tech firms are having to calm down their salespeople.

statement.excerpt: Generative AI is the next step up — a trend with an actual product, a superficially-impressive doodad that can sell cloud compute access and proliferate more software, even if the underlying technology is so remarkably unprofitable and unreliable that big tech firms are having to calm down their salespeople.

our_interpretation: The checkable core: by mid-2024, (a) generative AI was being sold and was driving cloud sales; (b) it was costly to run and had accuracy problems; (c) big tech firms were tempering their salespeople's expectations because of cost and reliability.
Part (c) is the distinctive factual claim, and the outcome rests mainly on it. 'Remarkably unprofitable' is treated as high cost relative to value, not as a specific loss figure.
Target period: the state of things when the post was written (first half of 2024).
criteria.support_condition: Credible reporting from H1 2024 that major cloud or tech firms told salespeople to temper generative AI expectations because of cost and accuracy limits, plus evidence the technology was being sold through cloud services.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that big tech firms were not tempering sales expectations in H1 2024, or that generative AI was clearly profitable and reliable then.
